## Safety contract

The preview and apply paths must share the exact same selector implementation. Preview returns the prospective immutable acknowledgement coordinates, counts, omissions, and recovery/apply command but writes no item, workspace, or history state. Apply records normal provenance and remains auditable.

## Empty-selection contract

Zero actionable coordinates is a successful, truthful no-op unless the caller selected a strict mode that explicitly makes no-match an error. The output must distinguish no match from malformed input, tracker corruption, and already-acknowledged coordinates.

## Scope

This is specific to history-author-acknowledge. It complements the broader update-many preview work but does not depend on it and must not be folded into a generic destructive-command rewrite.

GH-1028: history-author-acknowledge bulk mutation lacks dry-run and misreports empty selection

The irreversible history-author-acknowledge --all-actionable path can mutate every actionable attribution without a preview mode. When the selector matches zero streams it emits a misleading validation-style diagnostic instead of a truthful zero-selection result, making a recovery command unsafe to plan and hard to automate.

Add an SDK-native side-effect-free preview primitive used by CLI/MCP; expose --dry-run for --all-actionable with deterministic counts and coordinate samples under the output budget; define truthful zero-selection output and exit semantics; require explicit apply intent for the irreversible path without breaking documented compatibility; add unit, integration, acceptance, and disposable-directory manual proof; update runtime contracts, completions, and command docs.
project management = context management
Make immutable author-attribution recovery previewable, explicit, and automation-safe for both non-empty and empty selections.
Agents can plan a destructive recovery from CLI output without inspecting implementation code or risking an irreversible bulk mutation.
Operators can acknowledge the wrong attribution set at workspace scale, while automation cannot distinguish a healthy empty selection from a validation failure.
CLI, SDK action, contracts, MCP exposure, completions, docs, and tests share one preview/apply/zero-selection contract for history-author-acknowledge.
The new GitHub report exposes a safety hole in an immutable-history maintenance command; it must be modeled before any further bulk-recovery UX is consolidated.

pm CLI history-author-acknowledge command, current main at 996313a99bf7df942111cac40b8ada53107dcfe5; GitHub issue #1028 report

Run history-author-acknowledge with --all-actionable in a disposable tracker containing actionable unknown-author coordinates; observe that no dry-run/plan exists before immutable acknowledgement. Repeat where the selector yields zero actionable coordinates and inspect the diagnostic and exit behavior.

Bulk acknowledgement exposes a side-effect-free dry-run that reports the exact selected coordinates/count and recovery command; applying the mutation requires explicit intent. A zero-selection invocation returns a truthful machine-readable no-op result and documented exit semantics.

The command jumps directly from selection to irreversible acknowledgement, and an empty selection is diagnosed as though the tracker or input were invalid rather than reporting that no coordinates matched.
